environment.label: m7g.xlarge, 4 vCPU, 15 GiB RAM, EBS gp3

postgres.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

method.clientProcess: one Node process apart from Mason's, N node-postgres clients on its event loop
method.isolation: each engine measured with the other stopped: Mason closed while Postgres ran, Postgres's container stopped while Mason ran

queries.name: status
queries.title: orders and revenue by status, every row
queries.sql: SELECT status, count(*) AS orders, sum(amount) AS revenue FROM public.orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY status

queries.name: daily_tenant
queries.title: one tenant's orders per day, last 90 days
queries.sql: SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS day, count(*) AS orders, sum(amount) AS revenue FROM public.orders WHERE tenant_id = 42 AND created_at >= timestamptz '2026-07-03 00:00:00+00' AND created_at < timestamptz '2026-10-01 00:00:00+00' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

queries.name: top_customers
queries.title: top 20 customers by amount, joined to customers
queries.sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, sum(o.amount) AS total FROM public.orders o JOIN public.customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY total DESC, c.id LIMIT 20

queries.name: json_source
queries.title: orders by a JSON field (payload ->> 'source')
queries.sql: SELECT payload ->> 'source' AS source, count(*) AS orders FROM public.orders GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

queries.name: window_count
queries.title: paid orders in a 30-day window
queries.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM public.orders WHERE status = 'paid' AND created_at >= timestamptz '2026-09-01 00:00:00+00' AND created_at < timestamptz '2026-10-01 00:00:00+00'

queries.name: point_lookup
queries.title: one order by its primary key
queries.sql: SELECT id, tenant_id, customer_id, status, amount, created_at, payload, note FROM public.orders WHERE id = $1

clients.rowsWhy: the largest size the rows sweep measured under 60 s
